craft_evidence.owned: none: no owned factory, mill or workshop found. Meet the Makers says the brand "partnered with factories, artisans, and tailoring masters"; one robe is "Made on Madison Avenue in New York City" (1 style, no place detail)
craft_evidence.makers: Rochester Tailored Clothing (7 styles; since 1899), Hamilton Shirts (3; Houston, 1883), Waterbury Buttons (1; Connecticut), Mackintosh (2; Ireland). 11 of 376 clothing styles
craft_evidence.mills: Loro Piana 15 styles, Thomas Mason 10, Somelos 4, Joshua Ellis 3, Albini 2, Della Rovere 2, Drago 2, Mackintosh 2, Abraham Moon 1, American Woolen Mills 1, Bottoli 1, Harris Tweed 1. 48 of 376 clothing styles (12.8%) name a mill or maker
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed: PDP "Founded on Madison Avenue in 1938"; homepage "American, Since 1938". Partner heritage dated: Rochester 1899, Hamilton Shirts 1883, American Woolen 1853, Waterbury 1812 (Meet the Makers)
craft_evidence.process: partial: PDP bullets are specific (Full Canvas Construction, Real Horn Buttons, half-lined front leg, besom back pockets, margin stitching); Meet the Makers says staff visited the Rochester factory and "watched master artisans cut and stitch"; no process pages of the brand's own
craft_evidence.reasoning: Paul Stuart names makers and mills on product pages (Rochester Tailored Clothing, Hamilton Shirts, Loro Piana, Thomas Mason, American Woolen) but only on 12.8% of clothing styles, and owns no factory. Country of manufacture is stated on 65% of clothing styles (Italy 129, Canada 63, USA 17 of 245 statements). Heritage is dated and placed (1938, Madison Avenue), which fits a 3: names makers and mills, owns nothing.
